newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia unlikely to change rouble policy in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia unlikely to change rouble policy in 1997.

text.p: Russia's central bank is unlikely to make big changes to its exchange rate policy next year, Interfax news agency quoted a senior central bank official as saying on Thursday.
Under the current crawling peg exchange rate policy, which runs until the end of the year, the rouble should be trading in a 5,500-6,100 per dollar corridor on December 31 of this year.
"The current policy will be continued in 1997, only the band of the fluctuation rate will be changed," deputy chairman Alexander Potyomkin told Interfax.
The central bank will base its policy on the annual inflation rate, which will this year amount to 25 percent and will fall to 12 percent in 1997, Interfax quoted Potyomkin as saying.
